name: Eastern Wood-Pewee
facts: Call pattern: a slow, plaintive, slurred "pee-a-weee," given from before dawn until after dusk.
Habitat: the mid-level canopy of deciduous woods. Darts out from a perch to snap up flying insects, then returns.
Migration: long-distance. Winters in South America and arrives later in spring than most songbirds.
